verdict.oneLiner: Create a public connection in the developer portal and get OAuth credentials straight away. A security review only applies if you list it on the Marketplace.

approvalWait.note: You can create and use a public connection without listing it. Listing on the Notion Marketplace is optional. Notion reviews every listing and says to expect an email within 5-10 business days; listings can be rejected (for example brand or quality issues) and can be resubmitted after changes.

prerequisites.label: A Notion workspace to develop in
prerequisites.detail: Creating a connection asks for a development workspace. Notion's docs say internal connections require a workspace owner; they don't say whether public connections do.

prerequisites.label: Your OAuth redirect URI(s)
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URIs are configured under the OAuth configuration section of the connection.

prerequisites.label: A decision on installation scope
prerequisites.detail: Choose 'Any workspace' for a public connection. Installation scope is set once at creation and can't be changed afterwards.

steps.title: Open the developer portal and create a connection
steps.body: Go to the developer portal, select Connections in the Build section, then Create new connection.

steps.title: Pick 'Any workspace' as the installation scope
steps.body: This makes it a public connection that users in any workspace can authorize via OAuth. It can't be changed later; choosing specific workspaces means creating a new connection to list on the Marketplace.

steps.title: Add redirect URIs and capabilities
steps.body: Set the redirect URI(s) under OAuth configuration and choose capabilities such as read, update and insert content. Then copy the OAuth client ID and secret from the Configuration tab.
steps.agentCanHelp: Suggests the minimum capabilities for your use case.

steps.title: Implement the authorization flow
steps.body: Send users to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize and exchange the code at https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token. Store the token pair from each authorization.
steps.agentCanHelp: Writes the redirect, code exchange and token storage.

steps.title: Handle refresh tokens
steps.body: Refreshing generates a new access token and a new refresh token, so persist both every time you refresh.
steps.agentCanHelp: Implements refresh with atomic token-pair storage.

steps.title: Optional: list on the Notion Marketplace
steps.body: Listing details are managed in the Listings section. Public connections must pass a Notion security review before they are listed.

scopes.name: Read content
scopes.note: Capability chosen on the connection, not an OAuth scope string.

nuances.title: Users choose which pages your app can see
nuances.body: During authorization users select pages and databases in a page picker. It only shows pages they have full access to, and sharing a parent page shares its children.

nuances.title: Each user authorizes separately
nuances.body: Only the authorizing user can share pages with the connection. One user's grant isn't shared with the rest of the workspace.

nuances.title: Installation scope is permanent
nuances.body: Pick it carefully. Changing it means creating a new connection and new credentials.

blockers.title: API calls can't find a page
blockers.symptom: Requests for a page or database return not found even though the user can see it in Notion.
blockers.fix: The user didn't share that page in the page picker. Ask them to re-authorize and select it, or share a parent page.

blockers.title: Can't list on the Marketplace
blockers.symptom: The connection was created for specific workspaces.
blockers.fix: Create a new connection with 'Any workspace' installation scope.

agentCan: Write the OAuth redirect and code exchange
humanMust: Create the connection in the developer portal
Submit for Marketplace review, if listing

unknowns: Active setup time (10–30 min) is an estimate; Notion publishes no setup time and this was not timed hands-on.
Notion requires a workspace owner for internal connections; its public-connection guide does not state whether a public connection needs one.
Access-token lifetime is not published; Notion returns a refresh token and rotates it on refresh.
